title: Random 502s when traffic grows
briefing: Everything is fine at night. During the day users get intermittent 502s.

artifacts.logs: web.stdout.log shows workers being killed as memory usage grows.

options.text: Reduce the number of gunicorn workers and/or move to a larger instance
Raise the health check interval so fewer checks hit the app
options.why_wrong: Health checks are tiny. The memory graph shows saturation.

options.text: Restart nginx every hour with a cron job
options.why_wrong: The killed processes are workers, not nginx. This only hides the symptom.

options.text: Add a second listener to the load balancer
options.why_wrong: More listeners do not add memory to the instance.

explanation: Six gunicorn workers on a small instance use almost all available RAM. When memory is exhausted, workers are killed and requests become 502s.
lesson: Worker count is a memory decision. More workers can improve concurrency but can also exhaust RAM.
hints: Look at the memory graph and the SIGKILL message together.
Workers multiplied by memory usage must fit in RAM.
